intro: Every king had five names. Two of them are written in cartouches: the throne name, taken at the coronation, and the birth name. The throne name follows “King of Upper and Lower Egypt” (sedge and bee); the birth name follows “Son of Re” (duck and sun disk). Inside, the god’s name is written first out of respect.

kings.name: Ramesses I
kings.role: Father of Sety I, founder of the family. He reigned for only a short time; Sety honoured him in scenes on the west wall of the Hall, and his names appear in their texts.

throne.name: Menpehtyre
throne.meaning: Enduring is the strength of Re
throne.look: Sun disk and game board, like Sety I’s name, but with leopard heads (pehty, “strength”) instead of Maat.

birth.name: Ramessu
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him
birth.look: Sun disk, three fox skins and folded cloth: the basic “Ramesses” spelling.

kings.spot: Look in scenes where Sety I honours a deceased king on the west wall.

kings.name: Sety I
kings.role: Builder of the Hall. All his carving inside it is in raised relief, mostly in the north half and on the clerestory. He died before the decoration was finished.

throne.name: Menmaatre
throne.meaning: Enduring is the Maat of Re
throne.glyphsNote: As written at stop 6: sun disk, seated Maat, game board.
throne.look: A short, compact group: sun disk on top, seated Maat, game board at the bottom.

birth.name: Sety-merenptah
birth.meaning: He of Seth, beloved of Ptah
birth.look: The name includes a small seated figure of the god Seth. It is often followed by “beloved of Ptah” or, in some texts, “beloved of Amun” (Sety-merenamun).

kings.spot: His Menmaatre is the easiest royal name in the Hall to recognise. Try it at stop 6, marker 6.

kings.name: Ramesses II
kings.role: Sety’s son. He finished the Hall, converted the south half to sunk relief, and put his names on the central columns and almost everywhere else, sometimes over his father’s.

throne.name: Usermaatre-setepenre
throne.meaning: Strong is the Maat of Re, chosen of Re
throne.glyphsNote: As carved on the column in the photo: sun disk, user, Maat holding an ankh, adze, water, sun disk.
throne.look: Sun disk, the canine head on a staff (user), Maat, then the adze (setep) with water (n) and a second sun disk.

birth.name: Ramesses-meryamun
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, beloved of Amun
birth.look: Sun disk, three fox skins, folded cloths, plus the Amun group and the hoe (beloved).

kings.early: In his first year his names were shorter: Usermaatre alone, and Ramessu-meryamun. He settled on the final forms in his second year and had earlier cartouches in the south half recut.
kings.spot: User + Maat + adze = Ramesses II. You will see it on the twelve central columns and on most of the south wall.

citations.locator: Early and final cartouches; conversion to sunk relief

kings.name: Ramesses III
kings.role: Added inscriptions in a few places in the Hall, and built a small shrine against the outside of the north wall for visitors who came to pray to the Theban triad.

throne.name: Usermaatre-meryamun
throne.meaning: Strong is the Maat of Re, beloved of Amun
throne.look: Starts like Ramesses II’s name, but ends with the Amun group and hoe (beloved of Amun) instead of the adze and sun disk.

birth.name: Ramesses-heqaiunu
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, ruler of Heliopolis
birth.look: The Ramesses spelling followed by the crook (ruler).

kings.spot: If you see Usermaatre without the adze, check whether it is Ramesses III.

kings.name: Ramesses IV
kings.role: Filled most of the 134 columns with friezes of his cartouches and extra scenes: his names appear thousands of times. He also put huge cartouches and Horus names at the bases of the central columns.

throne.name: Usermaatre-setepenamun, later Heqamaatre-setepenamun
throne.meaning: Strong is the Maat of Re, chosen of Amun; later: Re is the ruler of Maat, chosen of Amun
throne.look: Look for the crook (heqa) next to Maat, and for “chosen of Amun”: the adze with the Amun group instead of a sun disk.

birth.name: Ramesses-heqamaat-meryamun
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, ruler of Maat, beloved of Amun
birth.look: The Ramesses spelling with the crook and Maat.

kings.spot: Rows of identical small cartouches on the column shafts are usually his. He changed the spelling of his name and recut some of them.

citations.locator: Ramesses IV’s cartouches on most columns

kings.name: Ramesses VI
kings.role: Took over some of Ramesses IV’s big cartouches at the bases of the central columns by carving his own names over them. Plaster hid the earlier names; where it has fallen, several names overlap.

throne.name: Nebmaatre-meryamun
throne.meaning: Re is the lord of Maat, beloved of Amun
throne.look: The basket (neb) next to Maat and the sun disk, with the Amun group and hoe.

birth.name: Ramesses-Amunherkhepeshef-netjerheqaiunu
birth.meaning: Re is the one who bore him, Amun is his strength, god and ruler of Heliopolis
birth.look: A long birth name; look for the Ramesses spelling at the start.

kings.spot: At the bases of the central columns, a cartouche with a confusing jumble of signs may hold two or three kings’ names at once.

citations.locator: Ramesses VI usurped Ramesses IV’s cartouches

kings.name: Herihor
kings.role: High Priest of Amun at Karnak who took royal titles in the temple. He added bands of text low down on walls and columns, connecting himself with Sety I and Ramesses II.

throne.name: First Priest of Amun
throne.meaning: His title as High Priest of Amun, written inside a cartouche
throne.look: A cartouche that holds a priest’s title (the flag “god” and the Amun group) instead of a normal throne name.

birth.name: Siamun-Herihor
birth.meaning: Son of Amun, Horus is raised up
birth.look: The Amun group and the falcon of Horus.

kings.spot: Low bands of text at the bottom of the walls; many are worn or lost.

citations.locator: Bandeau text of Herihor, translation

kings.name: Horemheb
kings.role: Built the Second Pylon, the gateway you walk through into the Hall.

throne.name: Djeserkheperure-setepenre
throne.meaning: Holy are the forms of Re, chosen of Re
throne.look: Look for the scarab beetle (kheper) with three plural strokes.

birth.name: Horemheb-meryamun
birth.meaning: Horus is in festival, beloved of Amun
birth.look: The falcon (Horus) with the festival sign.

kings.spot: On the Second Pylon gateway at the west end of the Hall.

citations.locator: Horemheb built the Second Pylon

kings.name: Amenhotep III
kings.role: Built the Third Pylon, the eastern end of the Hall, two generations before the Hall itself.

throne.name: Nebmaatre
throne.meaning: The lord of Maat is Re
throne.look: Sun disk, Maat and the basket (neb). The same three signs begin Ramesses VI’s name, so check what follows.

birth.name: Amenhotep-heqawaset
birth.meaning: Amun is satisfied, ruler of Thebes
birth.look: The Amun group with the offering table (hetep).

kings.spot: On the Third Pylon at the east end of the Hall.
